name: Serpentine Belt
summary: Not publishable yet. The N52 idler pulley number (11287535860) and the single-use tensioner bolt are corroborated, but the belt part number conflicts between retailers (11287549150 vs 11287628650/6PK1990), the tensioner number is ambiguous, tensioner bolt torque conflicts (22 Nm vs 25 Nm + 90 deg), and the only procedure found is one E82 forum post with no sourced tension-release tool size, lock-pin size or routing diagram. Engine is unconfirmed (N52B30 vs N51B30). Recommend pulling BMW ETK/repair data for the VIN before building this guide.
variantDependencies: Engine N52B30 vs N51B30 (SULEV): kits are listed as N52; N51 fit is described only generically by BimmerWorld.
xDrive vs RWD: Turner lists xDrive models in the description and 325xi/328xi/330xi in the table, notes to verify fitment.
A/C compressor runs on the same main belt and tensioner on N52 (Turner); belt length/part may differ with options (Turner notes exclusions for X5 with Adaptive Drive/4-zone climate).
Alternator pulley removal may need a special tool (BimmerWorld); depends on Bosch alternator.

tools.item: 16 mm socket (E82 poster: pulley under alternator)
Torque wrench reading from low values/in-lb plus builder's square or torque-angle gauge for the 90 degree step
Alternator pulley removal tool (CTA-8088 suggested for Bosch alternators)
Torx socket for M11 tensioner bolt (size not stated)
Belt tension release tool/socket size and tensioner lock-pin size

parts.item: Main drive belt, Continental in Turner kit ADK0022P
Main drive belt, 6PK1990 in BimmerWorld/INA kit
Tensioner number as labeled by BimmerWorld (same number is the kit number)
Tensioner bolt M11x65 Torx, single use

torque.fastener: Tensioner mounting bolt (N52, aluminum one-time-use per forum)
torque.value: 25 Nm + 90 deg (E82 posters) vs 22 Nm (5series thread, tensioner spring mounting bolt)
torque.conflicts: 1addicts E82 posts: 25 Nm (18 ft-lb) then 90 deg; 5series thread asks about 22 Nm and a poster states 25 Nm + 90 deg for N52 aluminum bolt. All forum, none OEM. N54 thread shows other numbers (40/38 Nm) - not applicable.

torque.value: MISSING (thread unresolved: 80 Nm vs 19 Nm asked, no answer)

specs.value: One belt drives alternator, power steering pump and A/C on N52 (BimmerWorld lists alternator/PS/AC; Turner says A/C on same belt); diagram not found
BimmerWorld: tensioner at every belt change, 40-60k miles; forum opinion differs
about 1.5 h in one E82 post

steps.title: Photograph belt routing
steps.instruction: Before removing, photograph or diagram the belt path.

steps.title: Relieve tension and remove belt
steps.instruction: Rotate the tensioner to slack the belt; slip belt off.
warnings: Tool size and lock-pin method not sourced.

steps.title: Inspect
steps.instruction: Fold belt ribs outward and look for cracks; check tensioner for play/noise.

steps.title: Replace tensioner/idler (optional kit)
steps.instruction: Remove tensioner and pulley; install the new unit with a new single-use bolt; kit instructions say remove the retaining disc on the back of the pulley.
warnings: Torque conflict, do not publish a number until resolved.

steps.title: Route new belt
steps.instruction: Seat the belt on the crank pulley by sliding in sideways; last loop on the tensioner pulley.
warnings: Check every rib seats in each groove before starting.

steps.title: Verify
steps.instruction: Start engine, check alignment, noise, charging.

safety: Disconnect battery or ensure engine cannot crank; keep hands clear of belt and fan.
Support torque-to-yield procedure properly; do not reuse bolt.
Battery disconnect may trigger need for registration only if battery replaced (not for belt).
missingEvidence: Authoritative belt part number for VIN (ETK).
Tensioner/idler bolt torque from BMW data.
Tension release tool size, lock pin size, Torx size, routing diagram, fan/intake access notes for E90.
Confirmation of N52 vs N51 and xDrive fitment.
